extracted.intended_audience: comics creators, small-press publishers, SPX attendees, and readers/researchers interested in comics awards
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, eligibility, nomination, and voting procedures for the Ignatz Awards (Small Press Expo festival prize) focused on indie and creator-driven comics. Includes award purpose, who/what is eligible, jury and voting process, and award categories (including additions/discontinued categories).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose / mandate
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ignatz Awards were designed to honor work that challenges popular notions of comics, highlighting indie and creator-driven comics rather than mainstream titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original mandate (as stated) was to set the Ignatz apart from 'mainstream' awards like the Eisner Awards by favoring creator-owned work and focusing more on work done by a single writer/artist (historical note; citation needed in article). Emphasis is on work that 'challenges popular notions of what comics can achieve, both as an art form and as a means of personal expression.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted creators / eligible type of work
rubrics_metrics.description: Awarded for outstanding achievements in comics and cartooning by small press creators or creator-owned projects published by larger publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award specifically recognizes small-press and creator-owned projects rather than mainstream corporate-owned comics; creators and works should align with the small-press/creator-driven ethos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications eligible for award consideration 'are published between July 1st of the previous ballot year and June 30th of the current ballot year.... Publication date is determined by date of distribution.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is strictly tied to distribution date falling within the specified July 1–June 30 window for the ballot year; submitters/nominees should use distribution date to establish eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination process (jury)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations for the Ignatz Awards are made by a five-member jury panel consisting of comic book professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A small professional jury selects the nominees for each category; the jury size is explicitly five members, implying a curated shortlist process before the attendee vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury anonymity and timing of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The jury panel remains anonymous (from both the public as well as each other) until the announcement of the awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anonymity of jurors is maintained through the nomination and voting period and only lifted when awards are announced; this procedural rule is intended to reduce outside influence and preserve the integrity of nominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juror self-nomination / conflict-of-interest rule
rubrics_metrics.description: After a 1999 controversy involving juror Frank Cho, jurors are now prohibited from nominating their own work. However, there is no prohibition of one jury member's work being nominated for an award by his or her fellow jurors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct self-nomination by a sitting juror is forbidden; nominations of a juror's work by other jurors remain allowed. The rule addresses conflicts of interest but allows peer nomination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting mechanism (festival ballot)
rubrics_metrics.description: As one of the few festival awards rewarded in comics, the Ignatz Awards are voted on by attendees of the annual Small Press Expo (SPX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners are chosen by a ballot of SPX attendees (and exhibitors as referenced in sources), making the award a festival-determined prize; the article notes that results are 'unique to the environment found at the Expo,' so outcomes reflect the expo audience rather than an external jury or committee vote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories (current and historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ignatz is awarded in categories including: Outstanding Artist; Outstanding Anthology (added in 2017); Outstanding Collection (added in 2017); Outstanding Graphic Novel (added in 2005); Outstanding Story; Promising New Talent; Outstanding Series; Outstanding Comic; Outstanding Minicomic; Outstanding Online Comic (added in 2001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awards have evolved over time—some categories were added (e.g., Online Comic 2001, Graphic Novel 2005, Anthology/Collection split 2017) and some discontinued categories (e.g., Outstanding Graphic Novel or Collection 1997–2004; Outstanding Debut Comic 2000–2008; Outstanding Anthology or Collection 2005–2016). Nominees and entrants should apply/expect consideration according to the category definitions and year-specific category availability.
